p.src: Now Cao Cao had decisively defeated Lü Bu at Dingtao. Lü Bu gathered the remnants of his army by the coast, where all his commanders rejoined him, intent on fighting Cao Cao once more. Chen Gong said, “Cao Cao’s forces are now too powerful to contend with. First find a secure place to settle; it will not be too late to return afterward.” Lü Bu said, “I wish to seek refuge with Yuan Shao again. What do you think?” Chen Gong replied, “First send someone to Jizhou to learn what is happening. Then we may go.” Lü Bu followed his advice.

p.src: Meanwhile, Yuan Shao in Jizhou heard that Cao Cao and Lü Bu were locked in conflict. His adviser Shen Pei came forward and said, “Lü Bu is a jackal and a tiger. If he gains Yanzhou, he will surely set his sights on Jizhou. It would be better to help Cao Cao attack him, thereby removing this threat.” Yuan Shao accordingly sent Yan Liang with fifty thousand troops to aid Cao Cao. A spy learned of this and rushed to report it to Lü Bu. Greatly alarmed, Lü Bu consulted Chen Gong. Chen Gong said, “I hear that Liu Xuande has lately taken charge of Xuzhou. We may seek refuge with him.” Lü Bu accepted his counsel and set out for Xuzhou.

p.src: Someone brought word of this to Xuande. Xuande said, “Lü Bu is one of the bravest warriors of our age. We should go out to welcome him.” Mi Zhu said, “Lü Bu is a savage beast, not a man to be given shelter. Take him in, and he will harm you.” Xuande said, “Had Lü Bu not attacked Yanzhou before, how could this commandery have escaped disaster? Now he comes to me in his extremity. How could he harbor any other intention?” Zhang Fei said, “Elder Brother, you are far too kindhearted. Even so, we must be prepared.”

p.src: Xuande led his followers thirty li beyond the city, met Lü Bu, and rode back beside him. They entered the reception hall of the provincial offices, exchanged formal courtesies, and sat down. Lü Bu said, “Ever since Minister Wang and I plotted the death of Dong Zhuo, I have suffered the upheaval caused by Li Jue and Guo Si and wandered through the lands east of the passes, where few lords would tolerate me. Recently, when the villain Cao Cao cruelly invaded Xuzhou, you came valiantly to Tao Qian’s rescue. I attacked Yanzhou to divide Cao Cao’s strength. But unexpectedly I fell into his treacherous trap, losing soldiers and commanders alike. Now I have come to join you so that together we may pursue great designs. I wonder what you think of this?” Xuande replied, “Governor Tao has only recently passed away, and there was no one to govern Xuzhou, so they asked me, Bei, to administer its affairs for the time being. Now that the general has fortunately come, it is only right that I yield the province to you.” He thereupon offered Lü Bu the official tablet and seal. Lü Bu was just about to accept them when he saw Guan Yu and Zhang Fei standing behind Xuande, anger on both their faces. So Lü Bu feigned a laugh and said, “I am but a man of brute courage. How could I serve as governor of a province?” Xuande offered once more. Chen Gong said, “A powerful guest must not overwhelm his host. Pray have no doubts, Governor.” Only then did Xuande desist. He then held a banquet in Lü Bu’s honor and had a residence prepared for him.

p.src: The next day Lü Bu returned the courtesy by inviting Xuande to a feast, and Xuande went with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei. When they were pleasantly warmed with wine, Lü Bu invited Xuande into the rear hall. Guan Yu and Zhang Fei followed them in. Lü Bu had his wife and daughter come out and pay their respects to Xuande. Xuande repeatedly declined the honor. Lü Bu said, “Worthy younger brother, you need not stand on ceremony.” Hearing this, Zhang Fei glared and thundered, “My elder brother is a scion of the imperial house! Who are you to dare call him your worthy younger brother? Come here! I will fight you for three hundred bouts!” Xuande hastily shouted him down, and Lord Guan persuaded Zhang Fei to leave. Xuande apologized to Lü Bu, saying, “My unworthy brother speaks wildly when drunk. Pray do not blame him, elder brother.” Lü Bu remained silent. Before long, the banquet ended. As Lü Bu escorted Xuande to the gate, Zhang Fei came galloping up with his spear leveled and shouted, “Lü Bu! I challenge you to three hundred bouts!” Xuande hastily ordered Lord Guan to restrain him.

p.src: Meanwhile, after pacifying Shandong, Cao Cao submitted a memorial to the court and was promoted to General Who Establishes Virtue and Marquis of Feiting. At the time Li Jue had made himself Grand Marshal, while Guo Si had made himself General-in-Chief. They acted without restraint, and no one at court dared speak against them. Grand Commandant Yang Biao and Minister of Agriculture Zhu Jun secretly memorialized Emperor Xian: “Cao Cao now commands more than two hundred thousand troops and has scores of able civil and military officers. If this man could be enlisted to uphold the dynasty and destroy the wicked faction, it would be a great blessing to the realm.” Emperor Xian wept and said, “We have long suffered the oppression of these two villains. If they could be put to death, it would truly be a great blessing!” Yang Biao submitted, “Your servant has a plan. First we must induce the two villains to destroy each other. Then issue an edict commanding Cao Cao to bring his army and kill them, sweep away their faction, and restore peace to the court.” Emperor Xian asked, “How is this plan to be carried out?” Yang Biao replied, “I hear that Guo Si’s wife is exceedingly jealous. If someone uses a scheme to sow discord through her, the two villains will turn upon each other.”

p.src: The emperor then wrote a secret edict and entrusted it to Yang Biao. Yang Biao secretly arranged for his wife to enter Guo Si’s residence on another pretext. Seizing an opportunity, she told Guo Si’s wife, “I hear that General Guo is having an affair with Grand Marshal Li’s wife and that they are exceedingly intimate. Should the grand marshal learn of it, the general will surely come to harm. It would be best, madam, for you to put an end to their meetings.” Guo Si’s wife exclaimed in surprise, “No wonder he so often stays away all night! So he has been committing such a shameless deed! Had you not told me, I would never have known. I shall guard against it carefully.” Yang Biao’s wife announced that she must return home, and Guo Si’s wife thanked her repeatedly before they parted.

p.src: Several days later, Guo Si was again preparing to attend a banquet at Li Jue’s residence. His wife said, “Li Jue’s nature is unpredictable. Moreover, two great powers cannot stand side by side. If he poisons you after the wine has begun to flow, what am I to do?” Guo Si was unwilling to listen, but his wife’s repeated entreaties finally kept him at home. That evening Li Jue sent over food and wine from the banquet. Guo Si’s wife secretly put poison into it before presenting it to him. Guo Si was about to eat. His wife said, “How can you eat food that has come from outside without testing it?” She first tested it on a dog, which died at once. From then on, Guo Si harbored suspicions.

p.src: One day after court, Li Jue insistently invited Guo Si to a banquet at his home. The banquet ended at night. Guo Si returned home drunk and happened to suffer a pain in his belly. His wife cried, “You must have been poisoned!” She hurriedly had liquid manure poured down his throat. Only after he vomited did the pain subside. Guo Si said furiously, “Li Jue and I undertook our great enterprise together, yet now, without cause, he seeks to murder me. Unless I strike first, I shall surely fall victim to him.” He secretly mustered the armored troops under his command, intending to attack Li Jue. Before long, someone reported this to Li Jue. Li Jue was also enraged and exclaimed, “How dare Guo Aduo act so!” He mustered his own armored troops and went to attack Guo Si. They fought chaotically beneath the city walls, taking advantage of the disorder to plunder the inhabitants.

p.src: Li Jue’s nephew Li Xian led troops to surround the palace grounds. He brought two carriages, placing the emperor in one and Empress Fu in the other, and ordered Jia Xu and Zuo Ling to guard the imperial conveyance. All the other palace women and eunuchs were forced to go on foot. As they were driven out through the Houzai Gate, Guo Si’s troops arrived. A storm of arrows was loosed, killing countless palace attendants. Li Jue charged after them from the rear, and Guo Si’s troops withdrew. The imperial carriages braved the danger and left the city, then were forcibly escorted straight to Li Jue’s camp without any explanation. Guo Si led his troops into the palace, seized all the imperial consorts and palace maidens, carried them off to his camp, and set fire to the palace buildings. The next day, when Guo Si learned that Li Jue had abducted the emperor, he led his army to fight before Li Jue’s camp. The emperor and empress were both stricken with terror. p.src: Now Guo Si's troops arrived, and Li Jue came out of camp to meet them in battle. Guo Si's army was worsted and withdrew for the time being. Li Jue then moved the Emperor's and Empress's carriages to the stronghold at Mei, placing them under the guard of his nephew Li Xian. He cut off the palace attendants, provisions failed to arrive, and all the courtiers showed signs of hunger. The Emperor sent someone to ask Li Jue for five hu of rice and five sets of ox bones to distribute among his attendants. Li Jue angrily said, “Meals are served morning and evening. Why ask for anything more?” He sent them rotten meat and spoiled grain, all so foul that none could be eaten. The Emperor cursed him: “How can this traitorous villain deceive me so outrageously!” Attendant-in-ordinary Yang Biao hastily memorialized, “Li Jue is cruel and violent by nature; now that matters have come to this, Your Majesty must endure him for the present and must not provoke his fury.” The Emperor bowed his head without a word, tears soaking his sleeves.

p.src: Suddenly, an attendant reported, “An army is coming to rescue Your Majesty, its spears and blades flashing in the sun and its gongs and drums shaking the heavens.” The Emperor inquired who it was and learned that it was Guo Si. The Emperor's heart grew still more troubled. Then great battle cries arose outside the stronghold. It was Li Jue leading his troops out to confront Guo Si. Pointing his whip at him, Li Jue cursed, “I have treated you generously. Why did you plot to murder me?” Guo Si replied, “You are a rebel. Why should I not kill you?” Li Jue said, “I am protecting His Majesty here. How am I a rebel?” Guo Si said, “You have abducted His Majesty. How can you call that protection?” Li Jue said, “Enough words! Neither of us shall use his soldiers; we two will fight alone to decide the victor. The winner may take the Emperor.” The two men thereupon fought before the battle lines. After ten bouts, neither had gained the advantage. Then Yang Biao came galloping up and cried, “Generals, rest your arms a moment! I have specially invited the assembled officials to come and make peace between you.” Li Jue and Guo Si each returned to his own camp.

p.src: Yang Biao and Zhu Jun gathered more than sixty court officials and first went to Guo Si's camp to urge peace. But Guo Si had all the officials placed under guard. They protested, “We came with good intentions. Why treat us in this way?” Guo Si said, “Li Jue may abduct the Son of Heaven, yet I alone may not seize the ministers!” Yang Biao said, “One abducts the Son of Heaven and the other seizes the ministers. What do you intend to achieve?” Guo Si flew into a rage, drew his sword, and made to kill Yang Biao. Only after General of the Household Yang Mi earnestly remonstrated did Guo Si release Yang Biao and Zhu Jun; all the others remained confined in the camp. Yang Biao said to Zhu Jun, “We are ministers of the state, yet cannot uphold our sovereign and rescue our lord. We have lived in this world in vain!” When he had spoken, the two embraced and wept until they fainted upon the ground. Zhu Jun returned home, fell ill, and died. From then on, Li Jue and Guo Si fought each other every day for more than fifty consecutive days, and none could count the dead.

Guo Si has already accepted the imperial command. What is your will?” Li Jue said, “I rendered the great service of defeating Lü Bu, and in four years of assisting the government have won many distinctions, as all the realm knows. Guo Aduo is nothing but a horse thief, yet he dares arbitrarily to seize the ministers and oppose me. I swear I shall destroy him! Look at my strategy and my troops: are they not enough to defeat Guo Aduo?” Huangfu Li answered, “Not so. In ancient times, Hou Yi of Youqiong relied on his skill in archery and gave no thought to adversity, thereby bringing about his own destruction. More recently, you saw with your own eyes the power of Grand Preceptor Dong. Yet Lü Bu, though favored by him, turned against him, and in a moment Dong's head hung above the capital gate. Clearly, strength alone cannot be relied upon. You, General, hold the highest command, bearing the axe of authority and the imperial credentials; your children, descendants, and clansmen all occupy eminent positions. The state's favor toward you can hardly be called ungenerous. Now Guo Aduo has seized the ministers, while you, General, have seized the Emperor himself. Which offense, in truth, is lighter and which is graver?”

Huangfu Li answered, “Not so. In ancient times, Hou Yi of Youqiong relied on his skill in archery and gave no thought to adversity, thereby bringing about his own destruction.
More recently, you saw with your own eyes the power of Grand Preceptor Dong. Yet Lü Bu, though favored by him, turned against him, and in a moment Dong's head hung above the capital gate.
Clearly, strength alone cannot be relied upon.

You, General, hold the highest command, bearing the axe of authority and the imperial credentials; your children, descendants, and clansmen all occupy eminent positions. The state's favor toward you can hardly be called ungenerous.
Now Guo Aduo has seized the ministers, while you, General, have seized the Emperor himself. Which offense, in truth, is lighter and which is graver?”

p.src: Li Jue flew into a rage, drew his sword, and shouted, “Did the Son of Heaven send you here to insult me? I shall cut off your head first!” Commandant of Cavalry Yang Feng remonstrated, “Guo Si has not yet been eliminated. If you kill an imperial envoy now, Guo Si will have just cause to raise troops, and all the feudal lords will aid him.” Jia Xu also urged him strongly, and Li Jue's anger subsided somewhat. Jia Xu then pushed Huangfu Li outside. Huangfu Li cried loudly, “Li Jue defies the imperial command and intends to murder his sovereign and enthrone himself!” Attendant-in-ordinary Hu Miao hastily stopped him, saying, “Do not utter such words! I fear they will bring harm upon you.” Huangfu Li rebuked him: “Hu Jingcai! You too are a minister of the court. How can you side with a traitor? ‘When the sovereign is humiliated, the minister must die.’ If Li Jue kills me, that is only my proper fate!” He continued cursing without cease. When the Emperor learned of this, he hastily ordered Huangfu Li to return to Xiliang.

p.src: Now more than half of Li Jue's army consisted of men from Xiliang, and he further depended on Qiang troops for support. Huangfu Li spread word among the men of Xiliang: “Li Jue is plotting rebellion. Whoever follows him becomes an accomplice to treason and will suffer no small calamity hereafter.” Many of the Xiliang men heeded Huangfu Li's words, and the army's morale gradually dissolved. When Li Jue heard of Huangfu Li's words, he was furious and sent the Tiger Guard Wang Chang in pursuit. Wang Chang knew Huangfu Li to be a loyal and righteous man, so he did not pursue him at all, but merely returned and reported, “No one knows where Huangfu Li has gone.” Jia Xu also secretly told the Qiang men, “The Son of Heaven knows that you are loyal and righteous and have endured the hardships of long warfare. He has secretly commanded you to return to your commanderies and will richly reward you hereafter.” The Qiang men already resented Li Jue for granting them neither ranks nor rewards. They therefore followed Jia Xu's words and all led their troops away.

p.src: Jia Xu also secretly memorialized the Emperor: “Li Jue is greedy and without strategy. Now that his troops are scattered and his heart is fearful, he may be baited with a lofty rank.” The Emperor accordingly issued an edict appointing Li Jue Grand Marshal. Li Jue rejoiced and said, “This is the work of the spirit invoked by the witch’s prayers!” He richly rewarded the witch, but gave nothing to his officers. The Cavalry Commandant Yang Feng was furious and said to Song Guo, “We have braved death and exposed ourselves to arrows and stones, yet our merit counts for less than a witch’s?” Song Guo said, “Why not kill this villain and rescue the Son of Heaven?” Yang Feng replied, “Set fire to the central camp as our signal, and I shall lead my troops in support from outside.” The two agreed to act at the second watch that night. But their plot was not kept secret, and someone informed Li Jue. Enraged, Li Jue ordered Song Guo seized and put to death at once. Yang Feng waited outside with his troops, but saw no signal fire. Li Jue personally led his men out and came upon Yang Feng; they fought chaotically through the camp until the fourth watch. Unable to prevail, Yang Feng withdrew his army and went over to Xi’an. From this time onward, Li Jue’s military strength gradually declined. Moreover, Guo Si repeatedly attacked him, and very many were killed. Suddenly a messenger reported: “Zhang Ji has arrived from Shaanxi at the head of a great army and wishes to reconcile the two lords; he declares that if either refuses, he will lead his army against him.” Li Jue seized the chance to make a show of generosity and was first to send a messenger to Zhang Ji’s camp accepting peace. Guo Si likewise had no choice but to consent. Zhang Ji submitted a memorial requesting that the Emperor proceed to Hongnong. The Emperor rejoiced and said, “We have long yearned for the eastern capital. If We may now take this opportunity to return, it will be the greatest of blessings!” An edict appointed Zhang Ji General of Agile Cavalry. Zhang Ji presented grain, wine, and meat to provision the officials. Guo Si released the high ministers and officials from his camp. Li Jue prepared the imperial equipage for the eastward journey and dispatched several hundred former imperial guards, bearing halberds, as escort.

p.src: The imperial carriage passed Xinfeng and reached Baling. It was autumn, and a sharp west wind suddenly arose. Suddenly loud shouts arose, and several hundred soldiers came onto the bridge and barred the imperial carriage, crying sternly, “Who goes there?” The Palace Attendant Yang Qi spurred his horse onto the bridge and said, “His Majesty passes this way. Who dares obstruct him?” Two officers came forward and said, “We have General Guo’s orders to guard this bridge against spies. Since you say this is His Majesty’s carriage, we must see the Emperor in person before we can believe you.” Yang Qi raised the beaded curtain high. The Emperor proclaimed, “We are here in person. Why do you not withdraw?” All the officers cried, “Long live the Emperor!” and divided to either side, allowing the imperial carriage to pass.

p.src: The two officers returned and reported to Guo Si, “The imperial carriage has gone on.” Guo Si said, “I meant to deceive Zhang Ji, seize the Emperor, and take him back into Mei Fortress. How dare you let him pass on your own authority?” He beheaded the two officers and set out in pursuit with his troops. Just as the imperial carriage reached Huayin County, earth-shaking shouts arose behind it: “The imperial carriage, halt!” The Emperor tearfully said to his ministers, “We have scarcely left the wolves’ den only to fall into a tiger’s jaws. What are We to do?” They all turned pale. As the rebel army drew near, a burst of drums sounded. From behind the mountain swept an officer at the head of over a thousand troops, beneath a great banner bearing the four characters “Yang Feng of the Great Han,” and charged into battle. It turned out that after his defeat by Li Jue, Yang Feng had led his army to encamp beneath Mount Zhongnan; now, hearing of the Emperor’s arrival, he had come expressly to protect him.

p.src: The battle lines were drawn up at once. Guo Si’s officer Cui Yong rode forth and loudly cursed Yang Feng as a traitor. Yang Feng was enraged. Looking back toward his ranks, he called, “Where is Gongming?” An officer wielding a great axe spurred his swift bay horse straight at Cui Yong. The two horses met, and in a single bout Cui Yong was cut down from his saddle. Yang Feng pressed the advantage and charged. Guo Si’s army was routed and retreated more than twenty li. Yang Feng then recalled his troops and came before the Son of Heaven. The Emperor commended him, saying, “You have rescued Our person; your merit is great!” Yang Feng bowed his head to the ground and gave thanks. The Emperor asked, “Who was the man who just slew the rebel officer?” Yang Feng brought the officer forward to bow beneath the imperial carriage and said, “This man is from Yang County in Hedong. His surname is Xu, his given name Huang, and his style Gongming.” The Emperor praised and rewarded him. Yang Feng escorted the Emperor to Huayin, where the imperial party halted. General Duan Wei presented clothing, drink, and food. That night, the Son of Heaven lodged in Yang Feng’s camp.

p.src: After his defeat, Guo Si rallied his troops the next day and attacked the camp once more. Xu Huang rode out first to meet him. Guo Si’s great army closed in from all sides, trapping the Emperor and Yang Feng at the heart of the encirclement. At the height of the peril, great shouts suddenly arose in the southeast, and an officer led his troops charging in at full gallop. The rebel host broke and fled. Xu Huang took advantage of the moment to attack and inflicted a crushing defeat on Guo Si’s army. The newcomer came before the Son of Heaven; he was Dong Cheng, a kinsman of the imperial house. The Emperor tearfully recounted all that had happened. Dong Cheng said, “Your Majesty, put aside your fears. General Yang and I swear to behead the two villains and bring peace to the realm.” The Emperor ordered that they make for the eastern capital without delay. The imperial carriage set out that very night and proceeded toward Hongnong.

p.src: Now Guo Si, returning with his defeated army, ran into Li Jue and said, “Yang Feng and Dong Cheng have rescued the Emperor and taken him toward Hongnong. If he reaches the lands east of the mountains and establishes himself there, he will surely proclaim our crimes throughout the realm and order the lords to unite against us. Then not even our three clans will survive.” Li Jue said, “Zhang Ji’s army now occupies Chang’an, so we cannot move rashly. But you and I can seize an opportunity to unite our forces, go to Hongnong, kill the Han sovereign, and divide the realm between us. Why should we not?” Guo Si gladly agreed. The two joined their armies and plundered along the road, leaving every place they passed stripped bare. Learning that the rebel troops had come from afar, Yang Feng and Dong Cheng wheeled their forces about and fought a great battle against them at East Ravine.

p.src: Li Jue and Guo Si conferred: “We are many and they are few. We need only overwhelm them in a confused melee.” Thereupon Li Jue advanced on the left and Guo Si on the right, their troops swarming over hill and field. Yang Feng and Dong Cheng fought desperately on both flanks and barely managed to escort the carriages of the Emperor and Empress out; the officials and palace attendants, the seals, registers, and canonical books, and all the imperial possessions were abandoned. Guo Si led his army into Hongnong and plundered it. Dong Cheng and Yang Feng escorted the Emperor north toward Shan, while Li Jue and Guo Si divided their forces and pursued. While Dong Cheng and Yang Feng sent men to negotiate peace with Li Jue and Guo Si, they also secretly conveyed an imperial edict to Hedong, urgently summoning the former White Wave commanders Han Xian, Li Le, and Hu Cai and their three armies to the rescue. Li Le too was a bandit who had gathered an outlaw following in the mountains and forests, but necessity now compelled them to summon him. When the three armies heard that the Son of Heaven would pardon their crimes and grant them offices, how could they fail to come? They mobilized all the soldiers in their camps, joined Dong Cheng, and together advanced once more to retake Hongnong.

p.src: At that time, wherever Li Jue and Guo Si went, they plundered the people, killing the old and weak and pressing the strong and able-bodied into their army; when they met the enemy, they drove these civilian conscripts before them and called them the “Dare-to-Die Army.” Thus the rebels’ might was immense. Li Le’s army arrived and joined the others at Weiyang. Guo Si ordered his soldiers to cast clothing and other articles along the road. When Li Le’s troops saw clothing strewn all over the ground, they scrambled to seize it and completely lost their formation. Li Jue’s and Guo Si’s armies attacked from all sides in a confused melee, and Li Le’s army was crushingly defeated. Unable to hold them back, Yang Feng and Dong Cheng escorted the Emperor northward, while the rebel army pursued from behind. Li Le said, “The danger is dire! Your Majesty, please mount a horse and go on ahead!” The Emperor said, “We cannot abandon Our officials and go.”

p.src: The whole company followed, wailing and weeping. Hu Cai was slain amid the chaos. Seeing the rebels close on their heels, Dong Cheng and Yang Feng begged the Emperor to abandon his carriage and proceed on foot to the bank of the Yellow River. Li Yue and the others found a small boat to ferry them across. The weather was bitterly cold, and the Emperor and Empress barely managed to support themselves as far as the bank. The bank was so steep that they could not descend to the boat, while the pursuing troops were about to arrive behind them. Yang Feng said, “Join several horses’ reins together, bind them around His Majesty’s waist, and lower him into the boat.” From among the crowd, the imperial kinsman Fu De came forward carrying more than ten bolts of white silk. “I found this silk amid the rout,” he said. “We can join the bolts together and use them to lower His Majesty.” Shang Hong, Colonel of the Marching Army, wrapped the Emperor and Empress in the silk and ordered the men first to lower the Emperor, whereupon he succeeded in reaching the boat. Li Yue stood at the prow with sword in hand, while Fu De, the Empress’s elder brother, carried her down into the boat on his back. Those stranded on the bank fought to seize the boat’s mooring rope. Li Yue hacked them all into the water. After ferrying the Emperor and Empress across, they sent the boat back to carry the others. All who struggled to board had their fingers hacked off, and their cries shook the heavens.

Li Yue replied, “You may escort His Majesty away; I shall remain here.”

p.src: Dong Cheng and Yang Feng then escorted the Emperor on his way. In secret, Li Yue sent men to conspire with Li Jue and Guo Si to seize the Emperor together. When Dong Cheng, Yang Feng, and Han Xian learned of the plot, they deployed their troops in the night and hurriedly escorted the Emperor toward Ji Pass. When Li Yue heard of this, he did not wait for the armies of Li Jue and Guo Si but led his own troops in pursuit. Around the fourth watch, he caught up with them below Mount Ji and shouted, “The imperial carriage shall go no farther! Li Jue and Guo Si are here!” Emperor Xian was terrified out of his wits, and fires flared up all across the mountain. Indeed:
